rule: Each call in a multi-line method chain is reported on the line of its own method name, not the chain's first line. | `[[T alloc] init…]` is `T#alloc` plus `T#init…` (the init runs on a T)
notes: call_type convention used throughout this corpus: a callee that is a member of a type (`T#m`) or a receiver-qualified guess (`recv.m`, `.m`) is `method`; a C function (bare name) is `direct`. Each send of the nested chain is on the line of its own selector. `alloc` is inherited from NSObject → `Builder#alloc` medium; the init runs on a Builder → `Builder#initWithName:` high. `build` is sent to the result of `initWithName:`, a call that takes a parameter, so it is a computed receiver (call result) → `.build`, low (the parameterless-member rule does not apply). A keyword selector split over two lines is one call `setWidth:height:` on the line of its first keyword (C7: the line of the callee's name).
